summary: Enclosed CDF lookout built 1978 to replace a 1930s lookout; registered 1999; still in active service; county listed differently across sources.

facts.design: Enclosed CDF lookout with a live-in cab with slanted windows on a steel tower

staffing.status: in active service (NHLR); staffing not stated

access.note: NHLR says the lookout is open to the public via a 14-mile road; a road guide describes a 1.2-mile unpaved 4x4 road at the end

corrections.why: The FLO county listing and the survey station record quoted on the weebly page both put the site in Trinity County; only the NHLR says Shasta. Editor should confirm before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved: the NHLR says Shasta County, while the FLO list and the 1954 NGS survey record say Trinity. The story attributes Shasta to the NHLR and reports the Trinity records; the correction above is proposed for editor confirmation.

The NHLR says the lookout is open to the public by a 14-mile road, while a road guide describes a 1.2-mile unpaved road from E County Line Road that needs a 4x4. Both are reported; the story flags the difference and advises checking conditions.
The May 1978 newspaper spells the destination 'Bully Shoup Mountain'; the register and survey use Bully Choop. The story treats the 1978 item as probably about this site.

sources.title: How to get by car to the lookout at Bully Choop Mountain in California

notes_for_editor: County is contested (NHLR Shasta versus FLO and survey record Trinity); the proposed correction needs your check. The record has no height and the NHLR gives only elevation, so no height_m. The road guide is a user-run site; treat its road details as low confidence. The 1978 newspaper's Bully Shoup Mountain is probably this site but the spelling differs. A 1954 photo of the tower (archive.org, Black Cards collection) turned up in search but was not read, so no photo is listed. Staffing is only 'in active service' per NHLR.
